content.title: Takeaways from Michigan Basketball’s win vs Saint Louis in NCAA Tournament
content.text: Mar 21, 2026; Buffalo, NY, USA; Michigan Wolverines forward Yaxel Lendeborg (23) drives the ball while defended by Saint Louis Billikens center Robbie Avila (21) in the second half during a second round game of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament at Keybank Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | Mark Konezny-Imagn ImagesThe No. 1 seed Michigan Wolverines took down the No. 9 seed Saint Louis Billikens 95-72 in the second round of the NCAA Tournament at KeyBank Center on Saturday in Buffalo.With the win, Michigan clinched a berth in the Sweet Sixteen for a second consecutive season and inched a step closer to winning the second national championship in school history.AdvertisementHere’s takeaways from the second round win.Michigan reaches Sweet Sixteen in back to back yearsAfter missing the NCAA Tournament in the final two years of Juwan Howard’s tenure, the Wolverines have returned to national prominence under head coach Dusty May — reaching the Sweet Sixteen in back to back years for the first time since 2021-2022. Michigan has now advanced to the Sweet Sixteen seven times in the past 10 seasons, which is a very impressive feat.Only two wins away from returning to the Final Four Michigan’s most recent trip to the Final Four took place in 2018, but the Wolverines are on the doorstep of returning to college basketball’s biggest stage. With just two more wins, Michigan would reach the Final Four for the ninth time in school history and third time in the last 15 years. There’s still a lot of work to be done but a spot in the national semifinals is within reach.AdvertisementYaxel Lendeborg bounces back in a big wayAfter suffering an ankle injury in the Big Ten Tournament, Yaxel Lendeborg didn’t really look like himself in the first round win. However, Lendeborg bounced back in a big way against Saint Louis with a game-high 25 points, highlighted by a trio of thunderous dunks — including a fastbreak poster slam that fueled a 17-6 run and essentially put the game out of reach.Aday Mara is in the midst of a memorable March runAday Mara was great in his first NCAA Tournament game at Michigan — totaling 19 points, seven rebounds, six assists and three blocks in the win over Howard. The Wolverines center was nearly as dynamic against Saint Louis, racking up 16 points, five rebounds, five assists and four blocks. Mara is playing at such an elite level right now and he appears to be in the midst of a memorable March run.Elliot Cadeau’s excellent performance was much-neededElliot Cadeau’s impact varies on a game to game basis, but he was excellent in the win over Saint Louis — going for 12 points, eight assists and four rebounds. Just moments after Saint Louis took a lead in the first half, Cadeau took over in the ensuing minutes by recording eight points, two assists and one block in less than four minutes to help the Wolverines regain momentum.Nimari Burnett keeps up pace from beyond the arcDespite coming up short in the Big Ten Tournament title game last week, Nimari Burnett was able to break out of a recent slump and that’s paid dividends in the last two games. Burnett scored 15 points on 5-for-6 shooting from the field in the first round win, and followed it up with 11 points on 3-for-5 shooting from three-point range to help Michigan advance to the Sweet Sixteen.AdvertisementAbility to avoid turnovers will be key moving forwardTurnovers have been an Achilles heel for the Wolverines this season (ranking 226th in the country with 11.9 turnovers per game), but Dusty May’s team took much better care of the ball to open the NCAA Tournament. Michigan committed 10 turnovers in the win over Howard, and finished with just nine turnovers against Saint Louis, which will be key to continue moving forward.Pair of big runs paved the way for double-digit winBoth teams were trading punches throughout most of the first half until Michigan put together a 14-3 run to create a little bit of separation going into halftime. The Wolverines held Saint Louis scoreless for nearly four minutes and extended the lead to 46-34. In the second half, Michigan used another explosive run to pull away and put the final touches on a double-digit win.AdvertisementMichigan is nearly unbeatable when winning rebound battleMichigan has been one of the best rebounding teams in the nation, leading the Big Ten with 29.1 defensive rebounds per game. The Wolverines are nearly unbeatable when they win the rebounding battle and that continued with a 42-27 rebound advantage in the win over Saint Louis. Now, Michigan is 32-1 when they record more rebounds than their opponents this season.The Wolverines continue to shoot the lights out from outsideThe Wolverines have been relatively inconsistent from beyond the arc throughout the season, but they have caught fire in two games in the NCAA Tournament. During the win over Howard, Michigan shot 11-for-24 from three-point territory and they followed it up with an even better shooting performance against Saint Louis – knocking down 11-for-23 from three-point range in the win.
